topics.label: Introduction to the Hallmarks of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the lecture's learning objectives and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks centered on the loss of growth control.

topics.label: Sustained Proliferative Signaling and Growth Control Evasion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in signaling pathways like Wnt, RTK/Ras/MAPK, PI3K/Akt, and TGF-beta drive independent proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Blocks in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells disrupt normal maturation in both hematopoietic lineages and colonic epithelial crypts.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the apoptotic pathway and the mechanisms by which mutations in p53, Bax, and BCL-2 prevent programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine telomere maintenance, telomerase activation mechanisms, and the stress-induced senescence pathways cancer cells must overcome to achieve indefinite replication.

topics.label: Reprogramming of Cellular Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the metabolic alterations in cancer cells, including aerobic glycolysis, metabolic rewiring across tissues, and the epigenetic consequences of oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction and Regulation of Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the necessity of new blood vessel formation for tumor growth, its onset during tumor progression, and its therapeutic regulation.

topics.label: Invasion and Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic covers the multistep metastatic cascade, dissemination pathways, diagnostic methods, seed-and-soil interactions, and genomic duplication in metastatic clones.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Closing Remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This topic closes the lecture with summary reflections on the hallmarks literature and invitations for student questions.
